selected_action.description: Disable or rotate credentials tied to the confirmed suspicious principal.
selected_action.recommended_next_focus: Use active key status and last-used activity to justify containment.
selected_action.title: Contain Suspicious Credentials

selected_evidence.summary: The affected principal has an active access key used shortly after the suspicious login sequence.
selected_evidence.title: Access Key Containment Review
selected_evidence.whyItMayMatter: This directly supports disabling, rotating, or reviewing credentials during containment.

prompt.title: Explain How The Access Key Evidence Supports Your Action
prompt.text: Explain how the access key evidence supports your selected response action. Connect key usage or rotation risk to the response decision.

learner_justification.transcript: I selected Contain Suspicious Credentials and used Access Key Containment Review. This access_key evidence is expected to act as strong support for the decision. I am checking whether the screenshot clearly shows the affected identity, source IP, event timing, service, status, and risk signal. If those details do not directly prove the response action, I would treat it as incomplete context and compare it with another evidence source.

vlm_output.visible_evidence_summary: Access key details for an IAM user showing active status, last used service, region, and last used date.
vlm_output.reason: The screenshot shows an active access key with a recent last used date, which supports the need to disable or rotate credentials tied to the suspicious principal.

security_output.reasoning: The evidence shows an active access key used recently, which directly supports the need to disable or rotate credentials tied to the suspicious principal.
security_output.justification_assessment: The learner's transcript correctly connects the evidence to the action by mentioning the active status and recent usage of the access key, which are key factors in deciding to contain the credentials.
security_output.recommended_next_focus: Investigate CloudTrail events to understand the full context of the suspicious login sequence and to confirm the exact actions performed using the compromised access key.
security_output.risk_of_wrong_interpretation: The learner might overread the evidence and assume that CloudTrail events are not needed, which could lead to an incomplete understanding of the incident. It's important to review additional logs to understand the full scope of the incident.

coach_output.feedback: Great work identifying the active access key! You're correct that this evidence strongly supports the need to disable or rotate the credentials associated with the suspicious principal. However, you mentioned investigating CloudTrail events, which seems unnecessary based on the current evidence. Instead, focus on reviewing the IAM console activities around the same period to get a more comprehensive view of the incident. This will help ensure you capture all relevant information before making any decisions about containment.
coach_output.next_turn_guidance: Next, take a moment to review the IAM console activities around the same period as the suspicious login sequence. This will provide a broader context and help you make informed decisions about containment.
